relationship: Moving a piston changes the volume of a fixed gas at constant temperature, connecting collision frequency and pressure to the inverse pressure-volume relationship.

learnerLoop.action: Compress a fixed gas, predict an expansion, keep three different readings, calculate a pressure target, then investigate freely.
learnerLoop.modelChange: Pressure is 600/V kPa; particle count and velocity magnitudes remain fixed at constant temperature.
learnerLoop.evidence: Piston impacts, pressure gauge, volume and recorded pV products all respond to the same volume state.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Revise a prediction, derive a new pressure or volume from the invariant, or collect another reading.

invariants: Pressure and volume satisfy the same constant product in the gauge, graph and calculation.
Constant temperature is represented by unchanged particle speed, not faster particles during compression.
Collision-frequency evidence changes with volume and stays distinct from particle-speed evidence.
Working assistance preserves the need to manipulate the piston and compare physical evidence.
safeAdaptations: Change target values, wording or working support within the supported volume range.
Add comparisons of pinned readings that test the inverse relationship.
nonGoals: Do not model changing temperature, changing gas amount or non-ideal gas behaviour.
Do not replace the piston investigation with a formula-only quiz.

prompt.description: One current model task and one short action prompt.

model.description: Pressure is 600/V kPa; particle count and velocity magnitudes remain fixed at constant temperature.
model.visibility: Always visible; later controls are progressively disclosed.

working.description: Consistent worked examples linked to the model precede required learner calculations; the same rows, quantities and units carry through.

evidence.description: Piston impacts, pressure gauge, volume and recorded pV products all respond to the same volume state.
evidence.visibility: In-place feedback; readings only in relevant steps.

completion.description: Advances only after the current model-derived criterion.
completion.visibility: Guided steps; absent in the open experiment.

volume.domain: 2 to 8 L, in 0.05 L increments by pointer and 0.25 L by keyboard.
volume.output: Chamber size, gauge pressure and reading table.

pressure.source: Actual gas volume; predictions are entered separately in the working card.

product.output: Checks that predicted 2.5 L gives 240 kPa.

modes.guided: Small ordered visual investigations, with model actions and in-place revision.
modes.experiment: Final open mode keeps all variables within the original conceptual model, comparison readings and reset.

dependencies: Enter the predicted pressure within 1 kPa of 100 kPa, then test an animated expansion from 3 L to 6 L. The gauge always shows actual pressure.
Record three distinct volumes, each showing the same product.
Calculate 600 kPa·L and 2.5 L before testing the piston against 240 kPa.
Ungated experiment: manipulate the full range, record and clear readings, and attempt new pressure targets.
implementation.completion: Every guided criterion is evaluated from actual model state. Continue never bypasses an unmet criterion. Restart returns to the first step; Back repeats a prior step.
limitations: This is the existing Physics/Chemistry cross-listed gas model, presented as a Chemistry prototype.
Eighteen representative particles illustrate collisions; the displayed pressure follows the ideal-gas invariant, not measured 2D simulation impulses.
Temperature 300 K and amount of gas remain fixed; no heating, non-ideal gases, or quantitative kinetic-theory simulation.
